PullRequest.Title: Warn before saving characters that the file encoding cannot represent
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #44505

## Problem

When a file is saved in an encoding that cannot represent some of its characters (for example `windows1252` set through `files.encoding` or an `.editorconfig` `charset`), iconv-lite silently replaces those characters with `?`. The user gets no warning and the original characters are lost on disk.

## Change

- `isLossyEncoding(value, encoding)` in `encoding.ts` round-trips the text (string or snapshot readable, chunk by chunk) through the iconv encoder and decoder and reports whether it changed. UTF encodings are skipped since they represent every character. The bundled iconv-lite (0.7) has no unencodable-character callback, so the check is done by round-trip.
- `TextFileEditorModel.doSave` runs this check on the snapshot before writing, unless `ITextFileSaveOptions.ignoreEncodingLoss` is set. If characters would be replaced, the save fails with the new `TextFileOperationResult.FILE_ENCODING_LOSSY` and nothing is written; the model stays dirty.
- The text file save error handler shows: "Failed to save 'legacy.txt': Some characters cannot be represented in the encoding 'Windows 1252' and would be replaced. Select 'Save Anyway' to replace them, or save with a different encoding." with **Save Anyway** (saves with `ignoreEncodingLoss`), **Save As…** and **Revert**.

As with other save errors, auto save does not retry until the user saves explicitly, so the notification is shown once rather than on every auto save.

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/textfile/test/node/encoding/encoding.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/textfile/test/browser/textFileEditorModel.test.ts`: 120 passing, 0 failing. New tests cover `isLossyEncoding` (table of encodings and texts, plus multi-chunk readables), a model save that is refused and then succeeds with `ignoreEncodingLoss`, and a save of representable text that is unaffected.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: clean.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
- UI scenario on a dev build: with `files.encoding: windows1252`, typing `Ω ≠ 🙂 ö` into `legacy.txt` and saving shows the error, the file on disk keeps its original bytes (`63 61 66 e9 0a`), and the tab stays dirty; Save Anyway then writes `… 3f 20 3f 20 3f 3f 20 f6` as before.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The production save path directly awaits this function, and there is no await or scheduling boundary inside its snapshot loop. Desktop and remote buffered writes previously awaited provider IPC between encoded chunks. The UI-thread blocking mechanism and linear scaling are statically established; the exact pause depends on document size and codec.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Workbench main-thread snapshot traversal, codec CPU, temporary encoded buffers and decoded strings, and full-text comparisons.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One uninterrupted O(N) encode/decode/compare pass per actual dirty non-UTF document save, with early exit only on a mismatch. Same-version saves are coalesced and saves serialize per model, but Save All starts distinct documents concurrently and their synchronous scans execute on the same thread.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Dropped frames and blocked editor input during validation, plus additional save latency before any file write starts.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The model immediately handed one snapshot to textFileService.write. On the normal desktop/remote buffered path, encoding was pull-driven and separated by awaited chunk writes; there was no full-file validation task before writing.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every non-bypassed save in a non-UTF encoding now performs a complete synchronous encode/decode/compare pass in the workbench before issuing the existing file write.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added loop at encoding.ts:289-298 synchronously calls encoder.write, decoder.write, startsWith, and substring until the snapshot ends. The added await at textFileEditorModel.ts:1043 requires that entire loop to finish before textFileService.write at line 1053 can start.
Findings.Title: Time-slice the encoding-loss check before saving large files
Findings.Impact: Saving or auto-saving a multi-megabyte Windows-1252/Shift-JIS document containing entirely representable text blocks typing and rendering for the full validation pass, then encodes the file again for writing. Save All can run these scans back-to-back for distinct dirty files. UTF encodings and Save Anyway bypass the scan.
Findings.Evidence: TextFileEditorModel.doSaveSequential calls isLossyEncoding before write (textFileEditorModel.ts:1041-1053). After the module-load await, isLossyEncoding consumes the entire readable synchronously (encoding.ts:276-303). Previously toEncodeReadable encoded lazily in read() (encoding.ts:217-263), and FileService.doWriteReadableBufferedQueued awaited doWriteBuffer per chunk (fileService.ts:1425-1446); the desktop provider forwards writes over IPC. The new validation adds a full-file uninterrupted renderer task even on that buffered path.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep validation before writing, but perform it in a worker or in bounded character/time slices with actual event-loop yields, preserving the captured snapshot and encoding. Do not rely solely on snapshot chunk boundaries, since a returned piece can itself be large.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicit save, auto-save, and Save All for UTF-8/UTF-16 documents
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Save participants finish, two snapshots are captured, the added encoding resolution and UTF fast path finish, then the existing encoded write completes before the model becomes saved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate and write file contents through the existing desktop/remote filesystem provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged O(1) metadata operations plus one logical write per saved resource; buffered providers perform open/close and O(K) chunk-write IPC calls, where K is the emitted encoded chunk count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same write boundaries and chunk cardinality occurred, with one snapshot and without the added pre-write UTF fast-path check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save awaits completion and final metadata resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One actual dirty-document save after same-version coalescing; snapshot construction scales with piece-tree node count, not a full text clone. UTF validation does not consume document text.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Saves serialize per model and repeated saves of the same version join. Save All deduplicates editors and starts distinct non-untitled editors in parallel; UTF fast paths contain no full-file validation loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: UTF-8 requires no iconv load. UTF-16/BOM encoding validation and writing reuse the promise-cached iconv module. The added encoding resolution repeats in-memory override/validation work, not disk reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the UTF early return, snapshot implementation, and unchanged provider call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional piece-reference snapshot traversal is established, but its independent user-visible magnitude is not established; no full-content copy or extra filesystem access was found on the UTF check.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate high-confidence regression beyond bounded extra snapshot/encoding-resolution overhead; the reported full-file validation problem excludes UTF encodings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful save or auto-save of a large legacy-encoded document, including Save All
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After save participants and snapshot capture, the entire synchronous encode/decode/compare pass must finish in the workbench before the first write can be issued. The subsequent write encodes the text again.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write encoded chunks to the local main-process or remote filesystem provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No additional provider calls: O(1) metadata/open/close operations and O(K) chunk-write IPC calls per buffered resource, with existing small-file peeking.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Encoding was pull-driven during the existing write; on the normal buffered path, awaited provider writes separated encoded chunks. There was no complete synchronous encode/decode preflight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All existing write calls are newly delayed by the complete synchronous preflight pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the bundled iconv module used for encoding validation, decoding, and writing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared import promise per iconv module path per workbench lifetime, not one load per document or chunk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy encoding validation and the actual write already required the same cached module.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold module loading is awaited during encoding validation; subsequent calls reuse the promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N characters per actual dirty non-UTF document save, or the sum across distinct dirty legacy-encoded documents in Save All. Representable text takes the full pass; mismatches can exit early.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-model save serialization and same-version joining remain intact. Distinct Save All requests start concurrently without a global limiter, but their synchronous validation loops execute serially on the workbench thread and can run back-to-back.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The iconv import is cached and coalesced by module path in amdX.ts. Existing encoding validation loads it before the new check if necessary. Warm modules/codecs do not cache validation results or eliminate the full-text scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the new unyielding loop and its awaited position before writing are explicit, and the previous buffered write yields at IPC boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. Pause length varies with file size, codec, hardware, and the number of distinct documents saved together.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity synchronous-ui-work regression at encoding.ts:289.

Scenarios.Scenario: Encoding-loss refusal followed by explicit Save Anyway
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Validation scans to the first mismatch or the end, throws before writing, and shows a notification. Save Anyway bypasses validation and performs the existing write.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Suppress the unsafe write, then optionally execute the ordinary write with ignoreEncodingLoss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero filesystem writes for the refused attempt; one existing logical file write, with normal provider chunking, if Save Anyway is chosen.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first attempt wrote the lossy contents immediately; there was no refusal or explicit confirmation retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The refusal notification waits for validation, while the subsequent explicit retry waits for the file write.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One scanned prefix per attempted document version; a mismatch near the end can require the entire document. Automatic attempts stop once the model enters error state; later explicit attempts can scan again.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-model sequentializer prevents concurrent writes. Save Anyway preserves that serialization and skips the second snapshot/check. No automatic retry loop is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Module imports are shared/cached. The error notification is keyed per model resource. Validation outcomes are not cached, but automatic retries are explicitly suppressed by TextFileEditorModel.save.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: early return on mismatch, bypass handling, and auto-save error guards were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mismatch position controls scan duration. Error-state suppression limits recurrence, so there is no evidence of an unbounded retry or notification storm.
Scenarios.Verdict: The synchronous validation cost is covered by the reported finding; no additional retry, boundary-fanout, or retention finding qualifies.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save As to a new/text target or an existing binary/oversized target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve or create the target, copy source content and metadata, validate the target snapshot, and save. For binary/oversized targets, the changed recovery initializes the target from source contents and obtains disk metadata without deleting the original first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve metadata for an existing target while initializing its model from the source snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: An uncached target has an existence check and one initial resolve/read attempt. The binary/oversized recovery now performs one metadata stat for buffer resolution instead of deleting the target and recursively repeating existence/create/resolve work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: On binary/too-large failure, delete the existing target, recursively re-enter Save As, check existence, create an empty file, and resolve it before copying source contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The stat and target model initialization must finish before validation and saving.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the selected target and revert the original source following successful Save As.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical target write on success, zero on encoding refusal; successful file-source Save As can additionally re-read the source once for revert.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same successful Save As stages existed; the new validation may prevent the write and defer source revert until confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Target write and then source revert precede successful completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source and one selected target per Save As. Source-sized model construction is O(N); resolving a binary/oversized target fails once before the replacement buffer path. Ordinary Save As targets retain their existing filesystem path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: EditorService executes Save As operations sequentially. Resolve calls join pending per-resource resolution, and target saves use the model sequentializer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved target models are reused. The model manager joins pending resolves per resource; supplying contents forces a buffer-based resolve. Encoding imports remain shared. Failed newly created models are disposed by the manager.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in boundary counts and the new stat placement; insufficient evidence for a distinct actionable performance finding beyond synchronous validation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The buffer-based recovery adds source-sized model initialization but removes destructive retry I/O. Without measurements, no separate net user-visible regression is established for this less common recovery path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding. Preservation of the target intentionally changes recovery ordering; existing I/O is not multiplied per source chunk or editor group.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recover from a refused Save As using Save Anyway, another destination, or Revert
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Save Anyway saves the retained target, optionally reverts the unchanged source, then replaces source editors. Choosing another destination completes a normal Save As before reverting the abandoned target. Revert resolves disk contents unless soft fallback is needed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Complete the deferred Save As and restore its source after confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One target save per action, followed by at most one source file re-read for revert. Untitled-source revert does not read a source file. Editor groups do not multiply this save/revert count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without refusal, the initial Save As immediately performed the target write and source revert. The new action defers the same stages until confirmation rather than duplicating them per editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The handler awaits save and revert before replacing editors.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discard unchanged contents left in the previously refused target, with a soft-revert fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After choosing another destination, at most one additional abandoned-target disk resolve; if it fails, soft revert adds no further file read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no retained refused target to clean up because the initial Save As wrote immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup runs after the successful alternate Save As and is awaited by the action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected source/target pair per explicit action. Untitled sources can appear in G editor groups; replacement iterates those groups, but the file save occurs once before that loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The target write and source revert are sequential. Editor replacements execute sequentially across matching groups. Source/target version checks suppress inappropriate cleanup, not additional background work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The retained target is looked up in the text-file model manager and reused. Opening/replacing editors can reuse its resolved model; no per-group repeated file save is present. If the target was disposed, recovery falls back to one normal Save As.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in action sequencing, model reuse, and absence of per-group write fanout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Group count and filesystem latency vary, but the traced file-boundary cardinality is bounded per explicit action. No evidence establishes a severe cleanup or allocation problem.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence performance regression: explicit recovery adds bounded necessary cleanup and preserves one save per target.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all eight changed files and every diff page against base 066b95e79643685c1bbbadec58f86b0d212bb1b6. Traced encoding validation, snapshot construction, save serialization/coalescing, Save All scheduling, module caching, local/remote provider boundaries, Save As recovery, and notification actions. Submitted one medium-severity finding for full-file synchronous legacy-encoding validation on the workbench thread. No concrete historical performance-regression fix was established, so no blame or regression-fix report was warranted.
